summary.intent: Execute Phase 27 (writable-shares-poc) end-to-end: implement API backend, owner UI, and recipient write actions for shared folders, then verify via human UAT.
summary.outcome: All 3 plans executed successfully. A critical gap discovered during UAT (files uploaded to shared folders lacked IPNS records) was diagnosed and fixed with a dual-key IPNS wrapping scheme supporting both recipient and owner edits. Phase checkpoint approved after full end-to-end verification.

repo: The cipher-box-ci-debug checkout does not have .env files committed — they must be copied from ../cipher-box/ manually each session.
The web app defaults VITE_API_URL to window.location.origin+'/api' when the env var is absent, causing it to hit port 5173 instead of 3000.
SDK package build order matters: core → sdk-core → sdk. The web dev server fails if SDK is not built first.
The addShareKeys API endpoint originally only authorized the share owner; write-share recipients also need to add keys for files they upload.
NestJS watch mode does not always pick up DTO @ApiProperty enum changes — a full restart is required before OpenAPI spec reflects the update, which blocks API client regeneration.
Background bash tasks spawned by Claude Code are killed when conversation context shifts; use detached processes (nohup/disown) for dev servers.

code.finding: Shared upload originally set fileMetaIpnsName: '' — no per-file IPNS record was created, making uploaded files unreadable.
Save handler used the owner's updateFile (useFolder hook) unconditionally — fails for shared files because parent folder is not in the owner's folder store.
API URL fallback logic uses window.location.origin+'/api' when VITE_API_URL is unset, which is wrong for local dev where API runs on a different port.
keyType enum was 'file' | 'folder' only; extended to 'file-ipns' to store per-file IPNS private keys wrapped per-recipient.
@ApiProperty enum must be updated alongside the DTO validator enum or OpenAPI spec (and generated client) won't reflect the change.

workflow: Dual-key wrapping pattern: when a shared file needs to be editable by both owner and recipient, wrap the IPNS private key separately for each party rather than relying on a single wrapping.
Per-file IPNS records must be created at upload time regardless of whether the upload originates from owner or shared-folder context.
After modifying NestJS DTOs with @ApiProperty enums, always restart the API fully before regenerating the API client — watch mode is insufficient.
OTP codes for testing can be retrieved directly from API server logs.

friction: PostgreSQL host IP changed mid-session (192.168.133.114 → 192.168.133.12), requiring .env recreation.
Background bash tasks were killed repeatedly by Claude Code's conversation context shifts, requiring multiple restarts and eventually switching to detached processes.
No .env files in cipher-box-ci-debug checkout — had to be manually copied from the sibling cipher-box repo.
SDK not pre-built in ci-debug checkout; web server failed on first start requiring manual build of core → sdk-core → sdk chain.
NestJS watch mode silently failed to pick up DTO @ApiProperty enum changes, causing API client regeneration to produce stale types and a confusing TypeScript error cycle.
The addShareKeys authorization gap required an API change mid-UAT, adding unplanned scope to the checkpoint resolution.
open_items: Files uploaded to shared folders before the IPNS fix (empty fileMetaIpnsName) are permanently unreadable — no migration or cleanup path exists for legacy shared uploads.
The 'file-ipns' share_key type is new and untested beyond the PoC — the key rotation and revocation paths have not been audited for this key type.
Shared file save path in updateSharedFileHandler fetches share_keys on every save — no caching; could be slow with many keys.
The addShareKeys authorization relaxation (write-share recipients can add keys) has not been audited for privilege escalation across different share types.
No regression tests were written for the shared upload IPNS creation or dual-key wrapping logic.
